full_judgment:
4. The defendant No. 8 contested the suit by filling written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. The case of the defendant No. 8 is that the defendants (others) are in possession of the suit land before the auction purchase under the Zaminder and after promulgation of SAT Act, 1950, they became direct tenant under the Government and having paid the rent to the Government, they are in possession of the suit land for more than 50 years. 

 16. After the SAT Act 1950 came into force, the Government has acquired all rent receiving interests vide Notification No. 4826 LR to 4836 LR dated 2-4-1956. Auction sale was held before the SAT Act came into force on 14-4-1956 and after that date all the rent receiving interest vested upon the Government instead of Zaminder or 3rd party rent receivers and as per section 3 of the SAT Act all tenants holding lands under any rent receiver became tenants directly under the government. Rent receiver, as defined in section 2(23) of the SAT Act means a proprietor or a tenure holder and includes a raiyat or a non agricultural tenant whose land has been let out. PW 1 stated in the cross examination that Probhat Chandra Das Chowdhury was the Zaminder and he has several tenants. Auction sale was held against Zaminder/rent receiver for non- payment of rent and therefore, the auction purchaser purchased rent-receiving interest and occupied the place of earlier rent receiver against whom auction sale was held. It further appears that the auction sale took place under the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation 1 S86 for arrear of rent. The certificate of the auction dated 22-1-1954 where it mentioned “বাকী পড়া মহালের নিলামী সার্টিফিকেট" and thus the plaintiff purchased rent receiving interest of Mohal and not any tenancy right under any landlord. PW 4 also admitted that plaintiff purchased rent receiving interest.
